heading: How a client finds the leader
text: 1. The load balancer calls GET /primary on port 8008 of each node. 2. Patroni answers 200 only on the leader. 3. The load balancer sends port 5432 traffic only to the node that answers 200. 4. For port 5433 the load balancer calls GET /replica. Only healthy replicas answer 200. The check runs each 5

heading: How failover works
text: 1. Each Patroni holds or watches a leader key in etcd. The key expires after 30 seconds (ttl). 2. If the leader stops, its key expires. 3. A replica takes the key and promotes its Postgres to leader. 4. The load balancer health check finds the new leader. 5. Clients must connect again. Open connecti

heading: The state file
text: In local mode, pgha keeps its state in one SQLite file: <state-dir /pgha.db, or the path in --db or PGHA DB. The file has mode 0600. All commands and pgha console use the same file. SQLite lets several pgha processes use it at the same time. The file has two tables: Table Content clusters One row pe

heading: Old secrets files
text: Older versions wrote <state-dir /<name .pgha.json. When pgha opens the state file, it copies each such file that it does not have yet and prints a note. It never changes or deletes the old file. After you check the copy (pgha state export --name <name ), delete the old file.

heading: `pgha state`
text: Command Meaning state path Print where the state is. state list List clusters with saved secrets. state export --name N Print the secrets of N as JSON, in the old file format. state import FILE --name N Save secrets from a JSON file. --force replaces saved secrets.

Removes access for all other roles (REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC). 4. Stores the password in the state file. Rule

heading: What changes with `--pgbouncer`
text: - Each node runs PgBouncer on port 6432, in front of its local Postgres. - The load balancer sends ports 5432 and 5433 to port 6432 on the nodes. - Connection strings do not change.

heading: PgBouncer settings
text: Setting Value pool mode transaction default pool size --pool-size (default 20) max client conn 2000 max prepared statements 200 auth type scram-sha-256

heading: Login check
text: PgBouncer does not keep a user list. It connects to the postgres database as the role pgbouncer and calls the function public.pgha user lookup. The first db create makes this role and function. The function does not return superusers or replication roles, so these roles cannot log in through PgBounc

heading: Connection limits
text: --connections N sets two things: Where What Effect Postgres ALTER ROLE ... CONNECTION LIMIT N Hard limit. PgBouncer pool size=N for the database Extra queries wait. Without PgBouncer, a client above the limit gets the error too many connections for role. The tool writes the limits to /etc/pgbouncer/

heading: What does not work in transaction mode
text: - SET for the session (use SET LOCAL in a transaction). - LISTEN and NOTIFY listeners. - Session advisory locks. - Temporary tables that you keep across transactions. Prepared statements work. The Go pgx driver works in its default mode.

heading: 17.1 Path 1: build new, then copy
text: What db import does: 1. Creates the database and login, the same as db create. 2. Checks that the target database is empty. If not, it stops. 3. Runs pg dump on the leader node against the old server. 4. Sends the dump to pg restore. The project login owns all objects. 5. Prints the number of tables

heading: 17.2 Path 2: adopt the server in place
text: Requirements: - A Hetzner Cloud server. Dedicated (Robot) servers are not supported. - Ubuntu or Debian Postgres packages (the pg lsclusters layout). - Exactly one online Postgres cluster, on port 5432, version 13 to 18. - The server is a primary, not a replica. - SSH access as root on its public IP

heading: Operations
text: Run these commands on a node, as root.

heading: Planned leader change
text: Use this before you restart or resize the leader.

heading: Change a Postgres setting
text: Patroni applies the change on all nodes. Some settings need a restart. patronictl list shows "Pending restart".

heading: Check PgBouncer
text: The password is pgbouncer password in the state file. cl waiting shows the clients that wait for a connection.

heading: Grow a volume
text: 1. Resize the volume in the Hetzner console. A volume can grow, not shrink. 2. On the node: resize2fs /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0HC Volume <id . 3. Do this for all nodes.

heading: Things to monitor
text: With --monitor or pgha monitor install, each node checks replication lag, free space on the data directory, the backup repository, PgBouncer cl waiting, a missing primary, a missing member, and local Patroni. Read section 16.

heading: Security
text: What the tool does: - No database port is open to the internet. - SSH uses keys only. With --tailscale, public SSH is closed. - All passwords are random (48 hexadecimal characters). - Postgres uses scram-sha-256 passwords. - Each project role can connect only to its own database. - Backups are encry

heading: Limits
text: - Backups, PgBouncer and Tailscale are set only at node creation. - up does not change resources that exist.
